items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, Scottsdale, Arizona, March 4, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I’m from the Gene Krupa, Buddy Rich, Louis Bellson school of drumming

ctx.x: You have to have two sets of clothes for before the gig and after the gig.

No I usually, if I work real hard, I might drop 3-4 pounds in an evening. It’s like I like to tell people that I’m from the Gene Krupa, Buddy Rich, Louis Bellson school of drumming, but I’m from the Elvin Jones school of perspiration, cause I do sweat a lot.
That’s saying something. Were you a typical bang-on-the-pots-and-pans-in-the-kitchen little kid?

items.title: Louie Bellson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: and some with Butch Miles, another great drummer.

ctx.x: So you played with Duke Ellington in the early ’50s and then you ended up playing with Count Basie. That must be a study in contrasts. Compare and contrast that. What was it like working with Count Basie?

Great. He was trying to lose weight and not drink. He knew that I’d go to the grocery store every day and stock up, because afterwards, a certain time of year, the restaurants closed. So every night for six weeks I’d hear a knock on my door – bam bam. I said, “Who is it?” “It’s me, Base.” Come in. We’d start talking about our experiences. Boy, you talk about experience, right there. They were funny. He was a real comedian. I’m trying to remember some of the things he said. One thing he said was – this was way…
